context.why: The review of the finished branch found six things. Two are serious and both were reproduced against the real code. The first is a privilege escalation: the Person administration form still renders the groups field for a non-superuser, so a Community Manager can put themselves in the Data Curator or Portal Administrator role and take every right the specification says that role must not hold. Narrowing is_superuser, is_staff and password closed three doors and left the one that grants the same rights by proxy. The second is a regression this feature caused: both plugin gates ask has_perm with a bare codename and no app label, which the permission backend refuses by design, so a Data Curator can no longer import into or publish any dataset - a capability the role declares, the migration exists for, and the administrator documentation promises. Four smaller findings travel with them.
spec_sections: Requirements / The role set (FR-002, FR-003, FR-004)
prior_decisions: The review's full text is specs/017-portal-roles/review-findings.json. Read SEC-001 and COR-001 in full, including their reproduction steps - both were probed against this tree and both give you the exact before and after.

auth.view_group is the discriminator the specification already supplies for who may change role membership: FR-002 gives it to the Portal Administrator and FR-004 withholds it from the Community Manager. Use it rather than inventing a new rule.
The backend refusing a bare codename is intended behaviour, pinned by tests/test_permissions.py. The call sites are what is wrong, not the backend - do not relax the backend to accommodate them.

A record's own contributors hold these rights as object-level rows and must keep working. The review verified that a contributor answers True for the dotted spelling too, because guardian splits the label and compares it against the object's.

acceptance.given_when_then: SEC-001. Given a Community Manager on the Person change form, When it renders, Then the groups field is absent as well as is_superuser, is_staff and password; When they POST a Data Curator group id for themselves or for anybody else, Then the membership is unchanged and they gain no rights. Given a Portal Administrator, Then groups is still offered and still saves, because FR-002 is their job. Given a superuser, Then everything is still offered. COR-001. Given a Data Curator and a dataset they did not create, When the import plugin and the publish plugin decide, Then both admit them - the gates ask with the app label. Given a person holding no portal role and no grant on that dataset, Then both refuse. Given a contributor who holds the object-level rows, Then both still admit them exactly as before. SPC-001. Given an administrator who reaches the delete page for a shipped role, Then they are told which role it is and that FairDM requires it, rather than meeting a bare refusal. EFF-001. Given reconciliation, When it resolves a role's declared permissions, Then it does so in one query per role rather than one per permission, with the same skip-what-is-missing behaviour. COR-002. Given the changelog, Then it records that the has_permission template tag no longer answers True for a member of a named group. And the navigation's administration-guide link is offered to somebody who can reach the administration interface, rather than only to somebody carrying the staff flag.
